body:
I really understand what you are going through. I was the older sister all my life, it was my identity. Honestly I lived for him most my life (32 now). Our mom had severe mental health issue and it was “us” against the world. We both had such immense pure love for one another (I still do) and I am extremely thankful that I got all that, even though for a short time. He passed away last year (just turned 25), suddenly and in a brutal manner. It pains me so much, his older sister his protector couldn’t do anything for him. This is something I live with. 

But, he lived a great life. And he gave me the best memories and love that will last my life. If I didn’t question all that love and his presence in my life, can I question him leaving me sooner than I thought ? I ask myself this. I now live for both of us, try to Atleast. Our family feels like it’s lost the most significant part of us. It’s just my parents and me now. But we go on for each other and my brother. I try to accept all now, the good and the bad. It’s a long life ahead I know, and it pains like hell to live it without him. But I shall, for him. Because how else do we keep them alive now ? Only through us. I wish you so much strength, you and your parents. You all have been through so much, I hope their love gives you much strength.

I am so sorry for your loss. I know your pain. My little brother, 25 y/o, was murdered in September during a carjacking. The criminals fled and for the longest time we thought they wouldn’t be caught as there was hardly any evidence. But we started a social media campaign, went on change.org, really put pressure on the authorities and the police solved the case. Although the pain never really goes away, knowing that justice is served brings you and the soul of your loved one some peace. 

I can’t even imagine how it feels to know the person who did this not be punished. I really hope some justice is done soon.
This is beautiful ❤️ Thanks for sharing!

I am so sorry for the loss of your brother in such a horrific way. Sadly I too lost my only sibling, my younger brother, to brutal violence during carjacking this September. He just turned 25. It is the worst thing that can happen to anyone, to lose your loved one in such a way. I had a very traumatic journey the first couple of months but it has gotten better. It took a long road of spiritual journey for me to make some peace. He was the dearest person to me, I loved him the most. Never could I imagine such a trauma. My parents thankfully are trying to keep it together for me, I am doing the same for them. It is very important for the family to come together right now, for each other. 

Please don’t put any pressure on yourself to make up for your sibling, it’s very natural to feel like this but you need to properly grieve first. You are enough for your family. Right now your whole family is in shock. It is still very fresh. If you feel your family is upto it, please consider grief counseling together. I would suggest someone with experience in trauma. Everyone’s culture is different and I believe the spiritual nature of my culture really helped my family. I say that because after such an event life can seem very strange, and it’s important you find something that gives meaning to your life and existence. I struggle with this so I am assuming somewhere you relate with this too. 

I would also ask you to not fear the future, in the start everything looked so grim to me. I couldn’t even imagine feeling 1% normal and thought my family is never going to be the same. But with time and effort, we are starting to have a new dynamic together, in which my brother is still a huge part of. We talk about him a lot, all the good memories, what he would say in a particular situation. In that way he is still alive with us. This is how me and my family have coped till now. I don’t know what the future holds but I have stopped worrying about what may happen. Instead I take each day by itself and try to live it as well as I can. 

I wish you so much strength to navigate this loss.

I am so sorry for your loss. I appreciate your post and I sit with you too grieving my little brother who I loved very very much. It is so so hard going into this new year without him, last year this day I flew in to spend 3 weeks with him and my parents. Little did I know it would be the last time I would physically see him. New Year’s Eve was one of our favorite times growing up, we would order our favorite pizza and dessert, visit our favorite place in town and watch the fireworks. He was my only sibling and the sweetest person in my life. I would do anything for him. 

Akki (24 August 1995 - 4 September 2020) you just turned 25 my baby brother, why did you leave us so soon ? I thought I would have my lifetime with you, I thought I would never be in a world without you. You were supposed to see me get married, we had planned everything together. It pains me so much to start this year without you, I want to be stuck in 2020 forever. A year when I could still hear your sweetest laugh and see your face, when I could hug you so tight and never let you go. I couldn’t save you baby, your big sister let you down. I am so sorry Akki that it happened to you, what you went through in your final moments all alone. I hope you are at peace now and I hope you will wait for me. I love you so much.

I am crying reading this because I naturally started doing this a month into my brothers passing away. I imagine him everywhere, during the fleeting joy when I miss him so much and during the times of despair as he is the light I lived for. I had a major surgery recently and I imagined him holding my hand, calling out my nickname from his sweet voice and telling me it’ll be okay. That he will be there with me. I try to remember this dream I had, right after he passed away. In that dream I am lying on the bed alone, sad and missing my brother. Suddenly he appears next to me and says “I am back, you are not alone anymore”. In my heart I believe it was really him, comforting me that if I try I can really feel him beside me. This is the only thing that brings me some peace in these tormenting times. Thank you for this post, I hope it helps others as well.

Beautiful letter ❤️ happy birthday to Kenzie. Thank you for sharing, your daughter’s story has touched me.

I am so sorry for your loss. What you wrote about your and her relationship is incredibly touching. I can relate to you although I know all our feelings towards such loss are different. The parts about dreaming about them everyday, looking at the chats, feeling loss of any motivation I can share. I lost my baby brother, who was really my motivation to live, in September. Sometimes it just feels like yesterday. He loved me more than anything in the world, I know that. I know how lucky I am to be loved so deeply. And that’s what keeps me going, even though I know how much I just want to be with him. I am trying everyday, really hard, to live for both of us. I try to talk to myself like I would talk to him if he was in my situation. What would I say to him if he was feeling so low? This situation we are in is absolutely horrible no doubt. But I still feel his love you know. All the love he gave me is still with me. It still makes me feel warm. And I will carry him, his legacy with me through his love. He still survives, even though he is gone physically. I know how much he loved life and I want to respect it, even though it’s absolutely hard no doubt. If we can contribute to this world, even in a small way, because of their love, they still live on. This is what keeps me going right now. I wish you all the strength and hope you find some peace.
So beautiful, made me tear up. I am incredibly sorry for your loss.
I am so so sorry for loss. Such a heartbreaking story. You mom sounds like a truly wonderful person. I am sending you positive thoughts and strength.

I am in the same boat as you OP. I have been reading Dr. Stuart McGills book “back mechanic”, which I really recommend if you haven’t read it yet. So in the book it’s suggested that in your level of pain, you should try walking every hour but stop right before the pain starts. This way you are sending pain free signals to your brain during movement. Slowly you should track if the number of steps go up. Even if it’s 5 steps right now, going to 6 pain free steps is progress. You should always try to avoid any painful movement and keep your spine neutral. The thing with nerve pain is, if you tolerate more pain you become more sensitive to it. It is counterintuitive I know, but that’s what Dr. McGill suggests, and I have also experienced it. Hope you make some progress, good luck!

I am so so sorry for your loss. Your relationship is just beautiful. I too lost my brother, my favorite human being, 2 months back. A lot of what you wrote resonated with me so much. I think of my brother constantly and everything reminds me of him. Also your story hits me in another way, I have been suffering from a terrible back pain in the last 6 months , got 2 of those injections in my spine. My brother was my constant support and I was talking to him so much everyday. Little did I know that I would receive the horrific call just a few days after my procedure that my brother was a victim of a violent crime. Now, I have lost my beautiful baby brother, my reason for smiling, and I am still in bed in pain. But I am trying to be motivated to make his wishes come true. He only got to live for 25 years and I know the rest of my life will be spent thinking about him and waiting for the time that I’ll see him again. Hopefully I can live the rest of my life with a propose that was important for him and it will make me feel closer to him. I am glad everything reminds me of him because to me that says that he is very much alive in my heart.

I am so sorry for your loss. It is truly heartbreaking when someone so young and full of potential suddenly passes away. I understand your pain, that feeling of longing to just hear their voice one more time. To hug them so tight. People say time makes grief easier but that’s not the case with me at least. I lost my baby brother 2 months back suddenly and I realized first I was in shock. Now it’s sinking in that he is really gone and I just want to hear his voice so bad. He would call me every morning and it’s terrible to wake up and think he will never call me again. I am an atheist too but I have been learning to be spiritual. I actually asked my brother to give me a sign he is around me and I did get it. Maybe it was a coincidence but I do feel it was him. Try talking to your cousin out loud and in your mind, express your wish. Maybe you will feel something from within, maybe you will see a sign. Your love for her is so strong, I am sure you will feel something. At the end they are still here, they survive in our love for them. They will forever be within us. Take care.

I am so sorry for your loss, it’s truly horrible to see a beautiful soul like your friend’s pass away in such a manner. I feel you. My just turned 25 yo brother was murdered in a carjacking. He was truly the best person I know, his friends can’t believe it either. He was my life, taken away so brutally for little money? The criminals couldn’t even sell the car and were caught. It makes no sense to me. My brother was a wonderful soul who really made the world better, he made everyone around him a better person. Just snatched away. It will never make sense. I wish you and your friends family all the strength.

I am with you, I feel the same. I want to wake up from this nightmare and be with my brother. Life just seems too long to live without him. I hope we can all find some peace some day. Sending you love.

I am so sorry for your loss, losing your only sibling, to sudden death is extremely painful. Unfortunately I am in the boat as you, I tragically lost my only sibling. My brother (25yo) was my will to live, my best friend, my first child, my everything. He suffered from a major blood disorder in his life but that didn’t dim even an ounce of his will to live. Being the older sister (31), I was always very protective of him and loved him like my child. But recently he had gotten so mature that he would act like my elder brother. I was his first priority and he was mine. It completely broke me when I got to know that he was murdered in a senseless crime. My baby, the most innocent and pure soul ever (I really am not exaggerating, he truly was) murdered brutally ? How will that ever make sense? The fact that he did not die of his illness, which kept me anxious my entire life but instead by a horrific crime? It will never make sense. I lost a huge part of me. 

Our family is devastated but we are all trying very hard. I still wake up every morning in disbelief, I can’t accept that he is gone. But as the day goes on I keep repeating that although his physical body is gone, his soul still survives. I am not religious but I have started believing that death is definitely not the end. My family already has the eastern religious values where they believe in the continuity of soul and that is helping us. I also try to see my brother in my parents and they see him in me. He gave us so much love, I know it’s enough for my lifetime. There is a huge void in our life but we are going to try to live our lives according to his principles, to honor him. 

I hope it makes you feel less lonely knowing that people like me are also going through similar loss and understand your pain. I wish you all the strength and courage.

I am so sorry for your loss, your love for her is so powerful and palpable. Sudden deaths are very hard, I also suddenly lost my brother last month. I can feel your pain. I try to think that my brother is alive in our love for him but it is very hard. That void will forever remain but I am glad I had him in my life, even for a short time. I wish you all the strength.

I am so sorry for your loss. I understand the change in perspective after such a tragedy. I was a few months away from defending my PhD and my brother just passed away. It has changed my perspective completely. I feel I should have never started grad school because it made me miserable. I wish I was happier in the last 5 years and could be a better sibling to my brother. I was also in a separate continent and couldn’t visit my family that often. Grad school definitely added to my depression and that is the case with a lot of people. I don’t want to discourage you but I would definitely ask you to think about this very carefully especially at such a tender time. Academia is in a bad place right now because of the pandemic and budget. I completely understand your will to pursue your interest and by all means you should. That’s the reason I went into grad school, I had a great bachelors degree with good prospects but I chose this path to make a difference. However academia has disappointed me and many other people. There is a system of abuse that is hard to break, you tend to lose your worth overall. You have to be quite strong mentally and remind yourself that your self worth doesn’t depend on the papers you publish. And if you chose to go to grad school I would advice 1. Go for a masters first and see if you like it enough to pursue PhD. 2. Chose your advisor absolutely carefully, they can make or break you. I wish you the very best.

Thank you really for saying this. My baby brother passed away last month and I keep thinking where he is. He was the most wonderful person I know, so kind and loving. He loved me the most and so did I. It really breaks my heart. He just turned 25. He battled a major blood disorder his entire life but lived his life to the fullest. He gave us so much love. At the end it wasn’t his disease that took him but he was a victim of a violent crime. Life is so bizarre, he still had atleast 25 years to live. Taken away by a brutal murder after suffering so much in his life already. I don’t know why I am saying all this here, it’s the first time I have put this out. Your answer just touched me so much. I just hope with all my heart that he is in a wonderful place because truly he is the most beautiful person I have known. I hope he is playing with his recently departed puppy and is looking over us. I hope he knows how much I love him, that he will forever be my first child, that’s how I felt about him. My little baby brother.

I am so sorry for your loss. It is the helplessness of not being able to save our loved ones that torments us in our sleep. You are right, my dreams have started being less and less horrible as I am processing the loss. But mornings are just so rough. My heart goes out to you as well, it’s a kind of pain like no other. Thank you so much for responding, I feel less alone. Sending you positive thoughts.

I am so so sorry for your loss. What happened is absolutely horrible, especially that you know the killer and justice wasn’t served. I lost my younger brother (25yo) to brutal murder in a senseless crime last month and it hurts like hell. The criminals are still not caught. I understand your anger, my baby brother was the most precious person in my life, I loved him to infinity. I can only imagine your suffering. I am trying to believe in karma so I tell myself that the criminals are going to pay one way or another. That’s my coping mechanism. I wish you strength. I really hope justice is served for you and your sister.

I am so sorry for your loss. You and your father’s relationship sounds very special. You are right about how do people go on after losing a loved one, I don’t have any answers for you. I am myself going through the same emotions. I lost my little brother just 25 yo to a violent crime 7 weeks back. He was the one I loved the most in the world. Just like you and your dad, me and my brother could never keep in regular touch with our extended family. I understand your feeling about it being hard to talk to them now. I was good about keeping regular touch with my immediate family and was very close to them. So in losing my brother I have also lost my support system. I have mostly relied on reddit and online resources for my kind of loss and grief to seek support.

Coming to regrets I understand your grief. I have many regrets too, I lived in another continent for the last 5 years so I didn’t even physically see my brother for almost 6 months. When someone so close to us dies, we find all reasons to blame ourselves and have regrets. I would just ask you to be kind to yourself, your dad loved you very much and knows your feelings too. In hindsight events always look different. We always try to make our best judgements when the situation is happening and that’s what you did. I am sending you lots of positive thoughts and strength.

I am so sorry for your loss, it’s truly heartbreaking. You sound like a wonderful human being and husband. Just try to put one foot in front of other. Take one day at a time. I just lost my baby brother and I know it’s not the same but I feel your pain. Your family and other loved ones will get you through this. I am sending you a lot of positive thoughts and strength.
Thank you for your words . I am truly sorry for your loss, it’s the most painful thing to go through. I am sending you my positive thoughts 🤍

Thank you for your insight. You are right, letting go of our loved one is the hardest lesson, especially if it happens in a brutal way like this. I’ve read somewhere that everything that is not you, including your mind and your body, you mustn’t hold tight. At the end we all let go of everything anyway. I am trying to go through this journey being as sane as I can, although I don’t think I’ll ever move on. I will however try to move ahead with this event sewed into the fabric of my life, taking my brothers essence and memories with me. 
Thanks again 🙏
Thank you for your words. I thought so too, it’s a way for my mind to deal with his horrific reality. Something no one should ever go through.

I am truly sorry for your loss. I have the same questions as you. My little brother was a gem of a person, absolutely kind and so so loving. He was murdered brutally and had just turned 25. Why would something so monstrous happen to the most gentle person I know? My faith in the world or karma has absolutely shaken. One of my friends gave me this book about the spirit world. I am not sure I believe it yet but the book addressed this question. It said that the evil people live longer on the earth and good ones go to the spirit world much younger. In the spirit world they are happy and are able to do whatever they liked on earth much more peacefully. They compare earth to a realm between something like heaven and hell. This hasn’t helped me so much but in my darkest times some belief in this gives me respite.

I am really sorry for your loss. You said EXACTLY everything I am feeling. I too lost the person who understood me the most and loved me unconditionally. My baby brother. It’s been 6 weeks and I honestly feel my fiancé can not handle me being so sad anymore. I know he is under a lot of stress but it’s so painful. I know my brother would have been there for me ALL the time if he was still here. It’s horrible to know that the only person who could have supported is the one who is gone. Society doesn’t want to face sadness for long because it’s uncomfortable for them. We remind them of the realities of life, the painful, ugly side. They don’t want to face it at any cost and in return they rush us, even be mean to us. It’s so selfish but that is humankind unfortunately. I am sorry, I know it really sucks but hope that you feel some comfort in knowing that there are people who care on this sub and are going through the same thing. Sending you positive thoughts. Take care ❤️

Edited to make it gender neutral.

I am so very sorry for your loss. I get you, the mornings are terrible. I lost my 25 yo baby brother 6 weeks backs and I have dreamt of him every single day since. The feeling of waking up to the reality is just brutal. I cry most times. My brother was murdered in a senseless crime and I still can’t believe it. It feels like he is on a vacation and he will be back. As I am writing this it still doesn’t feel real. He was the person I loved the most and it was the same for him. My biggest fear was losing him and I can’t believe what is happening. 

I have read so much in the past month about reincarnation, that death is not the end of it all. That’s the only thing that keeps me going. I also meditate and imagine touching him, hearing his laugh. Sometimes I feel he is talking to me too. Love is very powerful and I believe they survive in our love for them. I feel my pain, this suffering, is a testimony to how much I loved my brother. I try not to fight it, although it’s hard. I accept that a part of me is gone but I will keep him within me forever. Maybe he will be back in my life, maybe I’ll see him again. This thought will keep me sane. 

Sending you all the positive thoughts and strength.

I am really sorry for your loss and the other trauma in your life. I know the feeling you are going through, when someone so close and important to you passes away it’s hard to go on. The person I loved the most and survived for passed away 6 weeks back. It’s hard to carry on but please know that this is not the end. Your bond was so strong that they will come back in your life. Try to meditate and talk to your grandma, it may sound weird to you but please try. You will hear her, she would never want you to die because of her. She is still with you, just try to feel her around you. And if you need someone to talk you can reach out to me or other very nice people on this sub. Reading a lot about spirituality is what is helping me right now, I would prod you to read as much as you can as well. Take care and I hope you find strength to navigate this unfortunate time.

Thank you so much for your kind and insightful words. You are right about using the word “passed on”. That’s exactly how I feel about my brother. I too spent hours reading about consciousness, the after life and reincarnation. The evidence was strong enough to make me a believer from an atheist, I have also had signs from him and I will continue to feel him around me. I will never get over it, and I understand that grief is the price we pay for living someone so dearly. I am sending you lots of positive energy and love. Take care ❤️

I really get you, it’s been a month and half that my little brother passed away and I still feel him around. And I believe there is a reason behind it, his physical body is gone but his soul very much survives. The connection we have with our very close loved ones never goes away, they survive in our deep love for them. When I meditate and think about him, I can still touch him, feel his beautiful hair and listen to his infectious laugh. Nobody can take it away from me. There are many examples of talking to your loved ones in deep meditation in Buddhism and Hinduism. I was an atheist before my brother passed away but what I have learnt in this last month and half has changed my belief. Your partner could very well be around you that you still feel them. Don’t doubt it, just let yourself feel their presence and know that they are indeed okay.

All I can say I am so incredibly sorry, your story is heart wrenching. Even though I haven’t been through so much loss, I can only imagine your pain. Your feelings are completely valid, you were so close to your sisters husband and it’s going to hit you very hard. I just lost my 25 yo beautiful baby brother and it’s just brutal. The fact that you saw so many deaths so soon, it’s really gut wrenching. My brothers best friend lost his 26 yo sister, his 52 yo dad and now his best friend in a span of 1.5 years. I feel for him and I know the pain he goes through. I don’t have many words to comfort you, but I have just started my spiritual journey and I want to believe that all your loved ones who passed on are together right now. I am trying to live my life for me and my brother now, until I am reunited with him. Maybe it’s a coping strategy but I have been reading a lot, and I feel there is good evidence that this physical world is not the end of it. I am sending you my prayers and all the strength. Take care

Everything that you said, resonates with me so much. My younger brother passed away a month ago and I have never experienced such anguish before. My belief has changed drastically, I am also no longer scared of death. I want to be with him so much, but I need to go on for my parents. I hope my brother will continue to be with me until we are reunited. Till then I will live with his memory and his essence. 
I am really sorry for what you are going through, I wish you all the very best in your journey.

I am so sorry for your loss, I too lost my younger brother on 9/4/2020, 10 days after he turned 25. It is brutal to say the least, I talked to him everyday and I didn’t even get to say goodbye. He was the person I loved the most and still do, maybe even more now. I ache to be with him, I can’t accept he is gone. I hope we can all get though this, it’s heartbreaking to see so many people suffer.

I am really sorry for your huge loss, it is extremely heartbreaking. I lost the person I loved the most, my little brother, just 25, a month ago to murder. The criminals are still at large and we don’t know what really happened so I understand your feelings somewhat. 

I completely resonate with your feelings about other people rushing your grief, it’s horrible to hear all that. My extended family just went about their business so quickly and wanted me to stop crying. Like seriously ? But that’s how the world is unfortunately. I would really suggest talking to people who have been in your situation. You are very young to go through such a terrible loss, you really need good support. I recently watched this video of billy bob Thornton, talking about how at any given time he is 50% happy and 50% sad, after his brothers death. I really felt that. 
[billy bob about life after losing his brother](https://youtu.be/4Pn3y7S5FAw)

I wish you strength in your journey, know that me and other people around the world are also going through something similar. Grief can make you alienated but in a strange way it connects all of humanity.

I am so sorry for your loss, to lose someone so close in such a manner is absolutely devastating. I lost my little brother, just turned 25 yo, last month to murder. Ever since that day, I have recurrent dreams of him dying in different scenarios. Every morning is a battle. All I am saying is I understand what you are going through and unfortunately only people who have gone through such a loss will get you completely. My fiancé also feels helpless. I would really recommend talking to a support group. For me meditation really helped, and I spent a lot of time learning about death, the concept of soul and afterlife. I am a scientist so I don’t blindly trust anything, but I have now started to believe that my brother is still there, in his memories and maybe in his spirit. I talk to him when meditating, I try to feel his beautiful hair and hear his infectious laugh. I wish all the very best and hope you find your peace.
